name: Peach Tissue Silk Saree
ragaNote: Bhairavi is sung at the close of a morning concert — tender, unhurried, a little wistful. This saree has the same light: blush tissue with a gold-washed border that catches sunlight rather than demanding it.
care: Dry clean only. Store folded in muslin, refold every few months.

name: Marigold Kanjivaram with Royal Blue Border
ragaNote: Hindol is the raga of spring and swings. Marigold body, a royal-blue korvai border and a pallu dense with zari — made for Pongal mornings and wedding receptions alike.
care: Dry clean only. Wrap zari sections in cotton before storing.

name: Aubergine Banarasi Katan Silk
ragaNote: Yaman is the first raga a student learns and the one masters return to at dusk. Aubergine katan silk with a broad gold border and a flash of magenta — classic, with confidence.
details: Gold zari border with magenta edge
care: Dry clean only. Avoid spraying perfume directly on zari.

name: Rani Pink Bridal Silk with Gold Buttas
ragaNote: Kalyani literally means auspicious — the raga sung to begin good things. Rani pink silk scattered with gold buttas, a temple border and a pallu heavy enough for the muhurtham photographs.
details: Pure silk with gold zari buttas
care: Dry clean only. Air it out after every wear before folding.

name: Ivory Organza Anarkali Set
ragaNote: Chandrakauns is a late-night raga named for the moon. Ivory organza, a full twirling hem and a sequin-dusted dupatta — for sangeets that go well past midnight.
details: Made to your size within 7 days
care: Dry clean recommended. Steam, don't iron, the dupatta.

name: Teal Georgette Tiered Maxi
ragaNote: Megh is a monsoon raga, sung to call the clouds. Teal georgette, a cinched waist and a tiered hem that moves like rain on a field — the easy piece in the collection.
care: Gentle hand wash in cold water. Dry in shade.

name: Pista Green Chanderi Tissue Saree
ragaNote: Todi is sung in the first hours after sunrise, cool and searching. Pista green tissue with a broad silver-gold border, light enough to wear from a morning pooja straight into lunch.
care: Dry clean only. Store folded in muslin, refold every few months.

name: Peacock Blue Kanjivaram with Magenta Border
ragaNote: Malhar is the raga said to bring the rain. Peacock blue that turns green as it moves, a magenta korvai border and a temple-gold pallu — the colour of a sky just before the first downpour.
care: Dry clean only. Store folded in muslin, refold every few months.

name: Royal Purple Brocade Silk Saree
ragaNote: Darbari Kanada was sung in Akbar's court after midnight — slow, grave and grand. Royal purple brocade with a gold-shot body, made for evening receptions and long dinners.
care: Dry clean only. Store folded in muslin, refold every few months.

name: Ivory and Red Korial Silk Saree
ragaNote: Raag Durga is bright and devotional, sung through the nine nights. Ivory silk with a deep red and gold border, the saree of Pujo mornings, sindoor khela and every new beginning.
details: Plain ivory body with woven pallu
care: Dry clean only. Store folded in muslin, refold every few months.

name: Sindoor Red Banarasi Katan Silk
ragaNote: Bihag is the raga of the wedding night, sweet and full of longing. Sindoor red katan silk from Varanasi with silver-gold buttis and a deep woven border — the one the family will ask to borrow.
care: Dry clean only. Store folded in muslin, refold every few months.

name: Copper Kanjivaram with Chevron Weave
ragaNote: Basant welcomes spring with a burst of colour. Copper-rose silk woven in a soft chevron, framed by a rani pink and gold border that glows in evening light.
care: Dry clean only. Store folded in muslin, refold every few months.

name: Haldi Yellow Lehenga with Blush Dupatta
ragaNote: Bahar is spring in full bloom. A sun-yellow flared lehenga with a crisp white blouse and a blush net dupatta edged in gota — made for haldi mornings and mehendi afternoons.
details: Blush net dupatta with gota border
Made to your size within 10 days
care: Dry clean only. Store the skirt hung inside-out in a cotton bag; keep the dupatta folded flat.

name: Lilac Chikankari Lehenga
ragaNote: Puriya Dhanashree is sung at sunset, when the sky turns violet. Lilac georgette lehenga with silver chikankari and sequins, a flutter-sleeve blouse and a long, soft trail.
details: Georgette with chikankari and sequin work
Made to your size within 10 days
care: Dry clean only. Store the skirt hung inside-out in a cotton bag; keep the dupatta folded flat.

name: Rose and Teal Bridal Lehenga
ragaNote: Kedar is a night raga of devotion, played at weddings across the north. Rose pink lehenga with zardozi florals, a teal velvet blouse and a heavy red dupatta for the pheras.
details: Two dupattas: net and heavy silk
Made to your size within 21 days
care: Dry clean only. Store the skirt hung inside-out in a cotton bag; keep the dupatta folded flat.

name: Mustard Silk Lehenga with Maroon Dupatta
ragaNote: Bilaval is a bright morning raga, the 'major scale' of Hindustani music. Mustard silk with paisley gota-patti, a velvet border and a maroon bandhani dupatta for daytime weddings.
details: Made to your size within 14 days
care: Dry clean only. Store the skirt hung inside-out in a cotton bag; keep the dupatta folded flat.
